142	  schema_version: "2.0"
143	  description: >
144	    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
145	    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
146	    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.
147	
148	  scoring_scale:
149	    element: 0–5
150	    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass
151	
152	  rubric:
153	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
154	    - id: 1
155	      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
156	      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
157	      sub_elements:
158	        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
159	          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
160	        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
161	          field: ["title", "description"]
162	        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
163	          field: ["keywords"]
164	        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
165	          field: ["page", "resources"]
166	        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
167	          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
168	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
169	
170	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
171	    - id: 2
172	      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
173	      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
174	      sub_elements:
175	        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
176	          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
177	        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
178	          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
179	        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
180	          field: ["download_url"]
181	        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
182	          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
183	        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
184	          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
185	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
186	
187	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
188	    - id: 3
189	      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
190	      description: >
191	        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
192	
193	        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
194	        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
195	        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
196	      sub_elements:
197	        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
198	          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
199	        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
200	          field: ["format", "encoding"]
201	        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
202	          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
203	        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
204	          field: ["variables"]
205	        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
206	          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
207	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
208	
209	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
210	    - id: 4
211	      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
212	      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
213	      sub_elements:
214	        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
215	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
216	        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
217	          field: ["is_deidentified"]
218	        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
219	          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
220	        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
221	          field: ["informed_consent"]
222	        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
223	          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
224	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
225	
226	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
227	    - id: 5
228	      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
229	      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
230	      sub_elements:
231	        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
232	          field: ["subpopulations"]
233	        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
234	          field: ["instances"]
235	        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
236	          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
237	        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
238	          field: ["instances"]
239	        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
240	          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
241	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
242	
243	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
244	    - id: 6
245	      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
246	      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
247	      sub_elements:
248	        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
249	          field: ["version"]
250	        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
251	          field: ["version_access"]
252	        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
253	          field: ["errata", "updates"]
254	        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
255	          field: ["updates"]
256	        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
257	          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
258	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
259	
260	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
261	    - id: 7
262	      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
263	      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
264	      sub_elements:
265	        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
266	          field: ["purposes"]
267	        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
268	          field: ["tasks"]
269	        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
270	          field: ["funders"]
271	        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
272	          field: ["funders"]
273	        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
274	          field: ["creators", "funders"]
275	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
276	
277	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
278	    - id: 8
279	      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
280	      description: >
281	        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
282	
283	        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
284	        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
285	        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
286	        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
287	      sub_elements:
288	        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
289	          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
290	        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
291	          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
292	        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
293	          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
294	        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
295	          field: ["software_and_tools"]
296	        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
297	          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
298	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
299	
300	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
301	    - id: 9
302	      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
303	      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
304	      sub_elements:

306	          field: ["known_limitations"]
307	        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"

309	        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"

318	    - id: 10

d4d_complex_proxy_rubric:
  schema_version: "2.0"
  description: >
    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.

  scoring_scale:
    element: 0–5
    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass

  rubric:
    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 1
      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
          field: ["title", "description"]
        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
          field: ["keywords"]
        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
          field: ["page", "resources"]
        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 2
      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
          field: ["download_url"]
        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 3
      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
      description: >
        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
          field: ["format", "encoding"]
        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
          field: ["variables"]
        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 4
      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
          field: ["is_deidentified"]
        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
          field: ["informed_consent"]
        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 5
      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
          field: ["subpopulations"]
        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 6
      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
          field: ["version"]
        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
          field: ["version_access"]
        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
          field: ["errata", "updates"]
        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
          field: ["updates"]
        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 7
      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
          field: ["purposes"]
        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
          field: ["tasks"]
        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
          field: ["creators", "funders"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 8
      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
      description: >
        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
          field: ["software_and_tools"]
        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 9
      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
          field: ["known_limitations"]
        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
          field: ["known_biases"]
        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
          field: ["anomalies"]
        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 10
      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
      description: >
        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
          field: ["publisher"]
        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
          field: ["citation", "doi"]
        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
          field: ["conforms_to"]
        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
          field: ["related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

16	id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3
17	name: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
18	title: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
19	description: >-
20	  The Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project, version 3.0.0, is a
21	  multimodal cross-sectional dataset covering 2,280 participants with and without type 2
22	  diabetes mellitus (T2DM), collected between 19 July 2023 and 1 May 2025 and harmonized
23	  across three United States data collection sites: the University of Alabama at
24	  Birmingham, the University of California San Diego, and the University of Washington.
25	  AI-READI is one of four Data Generation Projects funded by the NIH Common Fund
26	  Bridge2AI program, and the dataset was built to be "AI ready" so that machine learning
27	  research on the pathogenesis and salutogenesis of T2DM — the pathway from disease back
28	  to health — can proceed without further reformatting or preprocessing. Recruitment
29	  sampling aimed at an approximately equal distribution of participants across diabetes
30	  severity (no diabetes; prediabetes or lifestyle-controlled; controlled by oral or
31	  non-insulin injectable medication; insulin-controlled), self-reported race and
32	  ethnicity, and biological sex. Each participant completed pre-visit questionnaires, a
33	  single on-site visit, and a ten-day at-home monitoring period. The released data types
34	  are OMOP Common Data Model clinical tables derived from REDCap (laboratory results,
35	  survey responses, physical and vision assessments, cognitive and monofilament testing),
36	  12-lead electrocardiography in WFDB format, retinal photography, optical coherence
37	  tomography, optical coherence tomography angiography and fluorescence lifetime imaging
38	  ophthalmoscopy in DICOM, continuous glucose monitoring and wearable activity monitoring
39	  in Open mHealth format, and indoor environmental sensor readings following NASA ASCII
40	  file format guidelines for Earth science data. The release contains 356,343 files
41	  totaling approximately 3.82 TB and carries no protected health information; information
42	  on the sex and race/ethnicity of participants and on medications used has been removed
43	  and is held in a controlled-access version of the dataset. That controlled-access
44	  version, which is not the artifact this record describes, additionally holds five-digit
45	  zip code, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications, and traffic and
46	  accident reports, and is available only to scientists whose institutions have completed
47	  legal and privacy use agreements with the AI-READI research programme.

146	purposes:
147	- response: >-
148	    To create and publicly share a flagship, ethically sourced, multimodal dataset
149	    optimized for artificial intelligence and machine learning research into type 2
150	    diabetes mellitus, including salutogenic pathways back to health.
151	- response: >-
152	    To develop a foundational dataset in type 2 diabetes that is agnostic to existing
153	    classification criteria or biases and that can be used to reconstruct a temporal atlas
154	    of T2DM development and reversal towards health.
155	- response: >-
156	    To create a model and blueprint for developing large, scalable, AI-ready clinical
157	    datasets, including guidelines for project management, data collection, management and
158	    sharing that future Data Generation Projects can follow.
159	- response: >-
160	    To increase access to and quality of AI/ML research by recruiting and training
161	    personnel, including a year-long research internship programme at the intersection of
162	    biomedicine and AI.
163	
164	addressing_gaps:
165	- response: >-
166	    The ability to understand and affect the course of complex, multi-organ diseases such
167	    as type 2 diabetes has been limited by a lack of well-designed, high quality, large and
168	    inclusive multimodal datasets. A major barrier to AI in this area has been the lack of
169	    diverse datasets that are AI ready for training models; the AI-READI dataset is
170	    intended to fill that gap.
171	- response: >-
172	    A meta-epidemiological review of type 2 diabetes studies published from 2000 to 2020
173	    found that samples lacked racial and ethnic diversity. AI-READI recruits four
174	    race/ethnic groups in approximately equal proportions rather than targeting the
175	    demographic distribution of the US population, as an intentional step towards
176	    addressing that gap.
177	- response: >-
178	    Existing data sources such as claims data or electronic health records do not support
179	    the downstream AI/ML analyses the project targets; the acquisition protocol was
180	    designed across multiple domains (survey, physical measurement, clinical, imaging,
181	    wearable device) to enable analyses that are not feasible with those sources.
182	
183	tasks:
184	- response: >-
185	    Downstream pseudotime manifold analysis: an approach used to predict disease
186	    trajectories by learning from complex, multimodal data collected from participants with
187	    differing disease severity, from normal through to insulin-dependent T2DM.
188	- response: >-
189	    Development of artificial intelligence and machine learning models on balanced
190	    multimodal type 2 diabetes data, including multimodal model development.
191	
192	other_tasks:
193	- task_details: >-
194	    The dataset is deliberately hypothesis agnostic; no specific labeling was performed,
195	    because the dataset is aimed at facilitating multiple potential downstream AI/ML
196	    applications rather than one predefined task. The healthsheet records no formal
197	    guidelines for researchers who wish to define new tasks or create new labels.
198	
199	data_collectors:
200	- role: clinical research coordinator
201	  collector_details: >-
202	    Clinical research coordinators at the three data collection sites recruited, consented
203	    and enrolled participants, ushered them through the research visit, conducted study
204	    visits including collection of ophthalmic images, trained participants on continuous
205	    glucose monitoring and the fitness tracker, and ensured the return of study devices.
206	- role: research assistant
207	  collector_details: >-
208	    Research assistants conducted study visits including collection of ophthalmic images,
209	    provided training on the at-home devices, and were responsible for data upload and
210	    management from each clinic visit under the direction of the study coordinator or
211	    project manager.
212	- role: data manager
213	  collector_details: >-
214	    A Data Manager at each data site was responsible for quality control of all data
215	    before uploading to FAIRhub; data managers at UAB trained all research personnel at the
216	    three data sites and oversaw the certification process for coordinators.
217	- role: phlebotomist and laboratory assistant
218	  collector_details: >-
219	    Phlebotomists collected blood from research participants and laboratory assistants
220	    processed and shipped samples.
221	  notes: >-
222	    All research personnel who recruited, enrolled and collected data underwent training by
223	    the data manager at UAB, followed a detailed Manual of Procedures, completed mandatory
224	    institutional compliance training for human subject research, and were required to
225	    administer all protocol elements to at least three volunteer practice subjects before
226	    enrolling participants.
227	
228	acquisition_methods:
229	- acquisition_details: >-
230	    Directly observable measurements, including laboratory results from blood and urine,
231	    vital signs, electrocardiography, visual function testing, monofilament testing and
232	    retinal imaging, were obtained during the on-site study visit.
233	  was_directly_observed: true
234	- acquisition_details: >-
235	    Participant-reported data were obtained through pre-visit and on-site questionnaires
236	    covering demographics, depressive symptoms, diabetes distress and self-care, diet,
237	    smoking, alcohol, vaping and marijuana use, general health, social determinants of
238	    health, vision difficulties and eye care access, and current medications.
239	  was_reported_by_subjects: true
240	- acquisition_details: >-
241	    Verification of data entry was performed where possible, for example by
242	    cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or
243	    photographed by each study participant.
244	  was_validated_verified: true
245	- acquisition_details: >-
246	    At-home sensor data were captured automatically over a ten-day post-visit period by a
247	    continuous glucose monitor, a wrist-worn activity monitor and a custom indoor
248	    environmental sensor.
249	  was_directly_observed: true
250	
251	collection_mechanisms:
252	- mechanism_details: >-
253	    REDCap was used for collecting patient-reported questionnaire data and the following
254	    clinical data from the visit: medications assessment, vitals, visual acuity, contrast
255	    sensitivity, monofilament test results and complete blood count results. REDCap was
256	    also the interface for recruitment, screening and electronic consent.
257	- mechanism_details: >-
258	    A 12-lead electrocardiogram was recorded with a Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph
259	    while the participant sat in a reclining chair or lay supine, with the chair position
260	    (0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees relative to supine) recorded.
261	- mechanism_details: >-
262	    Retinal imaging used six devices: the Optomed Aurora IQ handheld non-mydriatic fundus
263	    camera; the iCare EIDON widefield TrueColor confocal fundus system; the Heidelberg
264	    Spectralis HRA OCT/OCTA; the Topcon Maestro2 3D OCT-1; the Topcon Triton DRI OCT; and
265	    the Carl Zeiss Meditec Cirrus 5000 Angioplex. Both eyes were imaged on each
266	    participant, under dilation except for the Optomed. Fluorescence lifetime imaging
267	    ophthalmoscopy was performed on a Heidelberg FLIO device, macula-centred.
268	- mechanism_details: >-
269	    Continuous glucose monitoring used the Dexcom G6, a real-time integrated continuous
270	    glucose monitoring system that records a blood glucose measurement every five minutes
271	    and was worn for ten days; participants were masked to the results during the
272	    monitoring period.
273	- mechanism_details: >-
274	    Physical activity monitoring used the Garmin Vivosmart 5 worn on the wrist for ten
275	    consecutive days, with a sampling frequency of five seconds; participants returned the
276	    device with a form recording which wrist it was worn on and their dominant hand.
277	- mechanism_details: >-
278	    Indoor environmental measurement used the LeeLab Anura, a sensor unit custom designed
279	    at the Karalis Johnson Retina Center, University of Washington, placed for ten days in
280	    a frequently used area of the participant's home, with the placement location recorded
281	    on return.
282	- mechanism_details: >-
283	    Cognitive screening used the Montreal Cognitive Assessment administered electronically
284	    on an iPad using the MoCA Duo application, exporting total score, section subscores,
285	    Memory Index Score and task completion times.
286	- mechanism_details: >-
287	    Visual function testing used an M&S Technologies Electronic Visual Acuity tester at
288	    four metres, the Mars letter contrast sensitivity chart, a 2.0 neutral density filter
289	    for mesopic conditions, and a Topcon KR 800 autorefractor; lensometers used across
290	    sites were the NIDEK LM-600P and the Topcon CL-200 and CL-300.
291	- mechanism_details: >-
292	    Blood pressure was measured with automatic oscillometric devices; the devices used
293	    across sites were the OMRON HEM 907XL, the Medline MDS4001 and the Welch Allyn 6000
294	    series vital signs monitor with a Welch Allyn FlexiPort reusable cuff.
295	
296	collection_timeframes:
297	- start_date: '2023-07-19'
298	  end_date: '2025-05-01'
299	  timeframe_details: >-
300	    Version 3.0.0 contains data from participants seen between 19 July 2023 and 1 May
301	    2025, spanning the pilot phase and the first two years of the main study.
302	  source_caveats: >-
303	    The BMJ Open protocol publication states that enrolment began on 18 July 2023 and that
304	    preliminary pilot enrolment ran from 18 July 2023 to 30 November 2023, with formal data
305	    collection beginning 1 December 2023. FAIRhub, the higher-ranked source, gives 19 July
306	    2023 as the start of the collection period, and that value is recorded here.
307	- timeframe_details: >-
308	    The overall project timeline spans four years, with one year for protocol development
309	    and training and years two to four for subject recruitment and data collection.
310	    Recruitment was reported in the BMJ Open protocol as continuing until 30 November 2026;
311	    the FAIRhub study record gives an anticipated study completion date of 1 January 2027.
312	    The healthsheet states that approximately 4% of participants are expected to undergo a
313	    follow-up examination in year four.
314	  source_caveats: >-
315	    Sources give two different figures for the size of the longitudinal arm. The FAIRhub
316	    healthsheet states that approximately 4% of participants are expected to undergo a
317	    follow-up examination in Year 4, while the FAIRhub README, the RO-Crate description and
318	    NIH RePORTER all state that longitudinal data will be collected from 10% of the study
319	    cohort. The FAIRhub healthsheet and README are the same tier 1 source, so the ranking
320	    does not settle the disagreement; both figures are recorded rather than merged.
321	
322	direct_collection:
323	- is_direct: true
324	  collection_details: >-
325	    Data were collected directly from participants at the three recruiting sites; this was
326	    active data collection rather than passive collection or secondary use of existing
327	    data. Recruitment pools were identified beforehand by screening electronic health
328	    records for diabetes and prediabetes ICD-10 codes among patients who had had an
329	    encounter with the sites' health systems.
330	
331	sampling_strategies:
332	- is_sample: true
333	  is_random: false
334	  is_representative: false
335	  strategies: >-
336	    The FAIRhub study description records the sampling method as "Non-Probability Sample".
337	    The study base is all patients aged 40 years or older who had a medical encounter
338	    within each health system site between 2020 and 2025; patients with T2DM and
339	    prediabetes were identified by screening electronic health records for ICD-10 diagnosis
340	    codes E11.X and R73.09 respectively. Participants were recruited in waves, with the
341	    composition and size of each wave influenced by the observed participation
342	    characteristics of race/ethnicity, gender, severity of T2DM and site; composition was
343	    monitored and adjusted by under- and oversampling groups as needed. All study groups
344	    were recruited from each site, but the proportion of each group varies with the
345	    demographic prevalence of that group in the site's geographical area.
346	  why_not_representative: >-
347	    The cohort is intentionally triple-balanced by race/ethnicity, T2DM presence and
348	    severity, and biological sex rather than matched to the demographic distribution of the
349	    US population, because balanced training data are considered critical for developing
350	    unbiased machine learning models. Participants are volunteers, so volunteer selection
351	    bias applies, and recruitment is predominantly urban and hospital-based.
352	  source_caveats: >-
353	    The healthsheet for version 3.0.0 states that the dataset "contains all possible
354	    instances", meaning all participants enrolled during the covered period, and answers
355	    "N/A" to the question about sampling strategy at preprocessing time. The study
356	    description in the same FAIRhub record gives the sampling method as a non-probability
357	    sample. Both statements come from the same tier 1 source and are represented together
358	    here: the released dataset is not a sample of the enrolled participants, but the
359	    enrolled participants are a non-probability sample of the study base.
360	
361	collection_notifications:
362	- notification_details: >-
363	    Every individual was aware of the data collection, because it was active collection
364	    directly from participants rather than passive collection or secondary use. Individuals
365	    in each recruitment pool were mailed a hardcopy invitation letter and sent an
366	    invitation email, both personalised with links, access codes and QR codes directing
367	    them into an online REDCap recruitment interface where they could read an overview of
368	    the research programme, expectations for participation and answers to frequently asked
369	    questions, and could request a call back from study staff.
370	
371	collection_consents:
372	- consent_details: >-
373	    Informed consent to participate was required before participation in any part of the
374	    protocol, including questionnaires. Potential participants were given the option to read
375	    all consent documentation electronically before their visit and to give consent with an
376	    electronic signature without verbal communication with a clinical research coordinator;
377	    they could also access the e-consent documentation in REDCap and decide at that point
378	    not to participate or to request additional information. Participants who did not
379	    consent electronically were consented in person at the start of the visit.
380	- consent_details: >-
381	    The approved consent form for the principal project site, the University of Washington,
382	    is published with the dataset documentation. The other clinical sites operated under IRB
383	    reliance and used the same consent form, with minor institution-specific language
384	    incorporated depending on individual institutional requirements; the State of California
385	    requires inclusion of the Bill of Rights in the consent form at UCSD.
386	
387	consent_revocations:
388	- revocation_details: >-
389	    Participants were permitted to withdraw consent at any time and cease study
390	    participation. Any data that had been shared or used up to that point would remain in
391	    the dataset; this is clearly communicated in the consent document.
392	
393	informed_consent:
394	- consent_obtained: true
395	  consent_type: >-
396	    Written informed consent, obtained for most participants remotely as electronic consent
397	    through REDCap by computer, tablet or smart phone, and otherwise in person at the start
398	    of the visit.
399	  consent_scope: >-
400	    Consent covers the full study protocol, placement of the resulting data in an
401	    open-source repository, and the sending of biospecimens to the study sample repository
402	    for use in future research. The dataset record classifies the consent as
403	    "ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised" and notes that the public version of the
404	    dataset may only be used for type 2 diabetes related research while a private version
405	    allows more generic use.
406	  consent_documentation: >-
407	    The University of Washington consent form used for the study is distributed with the
408	    version 3.0.0 documentation as a PDF.
409	  withdrawal_mechanism: >-
410	    Participants were permitted to withdraw consent at any time and cease study
411	    participation; any data that had been shared or used up to that point would remain in
412	    the dataset, and this is clearly communicated in the consent document.
413	  notes: >-
414	    The consent form was reviewed by a community advisory board, and a table was added at
415	    the beginning of the form clarifying which information would be publicly available and
416	    which would require an application and approval process.
417	
418	participant_compensation:
419	- compensation_provided: true
420	  compensation_amount: 200 US dollars
421	  compensation_type: >-
422	    A stipend for the study visit, paid once the final data are received and the study
423	    devices returned, typically at least two weeks after the visit; the payment is not
424	    prorated.
425	  compensation_rationale: >-
426	    Compensation was drawn from the NIH grant funding supporting the study. The same type
427	    and amount of compensation is offered to participants invited back for the year four
428	    follow-up visit.
429	  notes: >-
430	    The study also covers reasonable costs for parking, public transit or rideshare fees
431	    related to the study visit, and transportation assistance through rideshare services
432	    was offered to participants who reported barriers to travelling to study visits.
433	    Participants may incur unreimbursed transport costs where fees exceed 25 US dollars.
434	    Staff effort was supported by NIH award OT2OD032644 based on percentage of effort
435	    contributed, with salaries aligned to the funding guidelines at each site.
436	  source_caveats: >-
437	    The IRB protocol notes that the stipend amount may change in later years of the study
438	    depending on funding, with the IRB to be notified of any change.

440	participant_privacy:
441	- anonymization_method: >-
442	    Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the
443	    public release via the Safe Harbor method, along with information related to the sex and
444	    race/ethnicity of participants, to prevent stigmatization of findings.
445	  privacy_techniques: >-
446	    The at-home environmental sensor and the Garmin fitness tracker were specifically chosen
447	    with participant privacy as a primary concern: they do not capture video or audio, are
448	    not equipped with GPS location monitoring, and are not synced with participant-owned
449	    devices. A robust data dissemination system, a strict licence agreement and data
450	    watermarking are used for both the public and controlled sets to deter re-identification
451	    attempts; the license states that the data may be statically watermarked to identify the
452	    licensee and that licensees must not remove, obscure, alter or mask the watermarking.
453	    Results returned to participants after the visit, including the Dexcom report and
454	    laboratory test results, are sent by HIPAA-compliant encrypted email.
455	  reidentification_risk: >-
456	    The healthsheet records a theoretical risk of future re-identification. AI algorithms
457	    can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level
458	    identification, which is the stated motivation for the dissemination system, license and
459	    watermarking.
460	  data_linkage: >-
461	    Participant folders are named after the participant's ID number used in the study, and
462	    a participants.tsv file provides participant-level metadata including the recommended
463	    train/validation/test assignment.

584	relationships:
585	- relationship_details: >-
586	    All instances are part of the same prospective data generation project, AI-READI. There
587	    is currently only one visit per participant, so instances are not linked longitudinally
588	    in this release; the healthsheet states that approximately 4% of participants are
589	    expected to undergo a follow-up examination in year four of the project, while the

591	    from 10% of the study cohort.

593	    Within a participant, files are grouped hierarchically by datatype, then modality, then
594	    device, then participant identifier, so that all records for one person across the nine
595	    datatype directories are linked by the participant's study ID number. Retinal imaging
596	    covers both eyes for each participant.

648	- split_details: >-
649	    Version 3.0.0 ships a recommended split of the 2,280 participants into training,
650	    validation and test sets in 70 / 15 / 15 proportions (1,576 / 352 / 352). Because sex,
651	    race and ethnicity are not released with the public version of the dataset, the project
652	    team prepared the splits so that the validation and test sets are balanced as far as
653	    possible for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status (no diabetes, prediabetes or
654	    lifestyle controlled, oral medication controlled, and insulin controlled). The
655	    assignment for each participant is included in the participants.tsv file. The training
656	    set holds 1,576 participants (Hispanic 204, Asian 369, Black 343, White 660; 599 male
657	    and 977 female; no diabetes 600, lifestyle 384, oral 487, insulin 105; mean age 61.1 ±
658	    11.3 years). The validation set holds 352 participants (88 in each race/ethnicity group;
659	    176 male and 176 female; no diabetes 88, lifestyle 88, oral 109, insulin 67; mean age

661	    group; 176 male and 176 female; no diabetes 88, lifestyle 88, oral 90, insulin 86; mean
662	    age 60.5 ± 11.4 years). The healthsheet describes this as a new recommended split
663	    introduced with this version, aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using

824	anomalies:
825	- anomaly_details: >-
826	    In survey data, skipped questions and incomplete responses are expected.
827	- anomaly_details: >-
828	    In wearable data, improper use and technical failure such as battery failure or system
829	    malfunction are expected. The Garmin Vivosmart 5 had to be charged every two to three
830	    days, so there are gaps in the activity monitoring record.
831	- anomaly_details: >-
832	    In imaging data, patient uncooperation, noise that may obscure the images, technical
833	    failure such as system malfunction, and data transfer failures are expected.
834	- anomaly_details: >-
835	    Optomed Aurora fundus photographs are taken undilated with a handheld camera, so image
836	    quality varies from patient to patient and within the same patient.
837	- anomaly_details: >-
838	    Fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy takes longer than a standard Spectralis OCT
839	    and exposes patients to uncomfortable levels of light, so it is performed last in the
840	    visit and patients may not be at their best possible compliance. The device cannot
841	    handle more than one centimetre of movement during image acquisition, and unwanted
842	    signals such as background light or lens fluorescence cannot simply be subtracted
843	    because they are part of the same photon distribution as the useful data.
844	- anomaly_details: >-
845	    Heidelberg Spectralis imaging is operated manually rather than automatically, so quality
846	    issues may arise that lead to skipping the modality and missing data.
847	
848	missing_data_documentation:
849	- missing_data_patterns: Not all modalities are available for all participants.
850	  missing_data_causes: >-
851	    Some participants elected not to participate in some study elements. In a few cases the
852	    data collection device did not have any stored results or was returned too late to
853	    retrieve the results, for example because the battery died or the data were lost. In a
854	    few cases there may have been a data collision at some point in the process and data
855	    have been lost.
856	  handling_strategy: >-
857	    During data entry quality control, missing data that could be directly filled from other
858	    portions of an individual's record were filled, under the guidance and approval of the
859	    site principal investigator. No imputation of missing values is reported for the
860	    released dataset.

867	  mitigation_strategy: >-

869	    screening rather than from clinic referrals alone, and composition is monitored and

872	  bias_description: >-
873	    While the AI-READI cross-sectional database ultimately aims to achieve balance across
874	    race/ethnicity, biological sex, and diabetes presence and severity, the pilot and interim
875	    releases are not balanced across these parameters, and periodic data releases may not
876	    have achieved balanced distribution across groups while enrolment is ongoing.
877	  mitigation_strategy: >-
878	    Uniform data collection protocols were implemented for all subjects irrespective of
879	    race/ethnicity, biological sex or diabetes severity across all study sites, and three
880	    study sites were selected to ensure varied representation and minimize the potential for
881	    sampling bias. The recommended data splits balance the validation and test sets as far as

893	    participants speak, read and understand English may also have created challenges in

id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3
name: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
title: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
description: >-
  The Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project, version 3.0.0, is a
  multimodal cross-sectional dataset covering 2,280 participants with and without type 2
  diabetes mellitus (T2DM), collected between 19 July 2023 and 1 May 2025 and harmonized
  across three United States data collection sites: the University of Alabama at
  Birmingham, the University of California San Diego, and the University of Washington.
  AI-READI is one of four Data Generation Projects funded by the NIH Common Fund
  Bridge2AI program, and the dataset was built to be "AI ready" so that machine learning
  research on the pathogenesis and salutogenesis of T2DM — the pathway from disease back
  to health — can proceed without further reformatting or preprocessing. Recruitment
  sampling aimed at an approximately equal distribution of participants across diabetes
  severity (no diabetes; prediabetes or lifestyle-controlled; controlled by oral or
  non-insulin injectable medication; insulin-controlled), self-reported race and
  ethnicity, and biological sex. Each participant completed pre-visit questionnaires, a
  single on-site visit, and a ten-day at-home monitoring period. The released data types
  are OMOP Common Data Model clinical tables derived from REDCap (laboratory results,
  survey responses, physical and vision assessments, cognitive and monofilament testing),
  12-lead electrocardiography in WFDB format, retinal photography, optical coherence
  tomography, optical coherence tomography angiography and fluorescence lifetime imaging
  ophthalmoscopy in DICOM, continuous glucose monitoring and wearable activity monitoring
  in Open mHealth format, and indoor environmental sensor readings following NASA ASCII
  file format guidelines for Earth science data. The release contains 356,343 files
  totaling approximately 3.82 TB and carries no protected health information; information
  on the sex and race/ethnicity of participants and on medications used has been removed
  and is held in a controlled-access version of the dataset. That controlled-access
  version, which is not the artifact this record describes, additionally holds five-digit
  zip code, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications, and traffic and
  accident reports, and is available only to scientists whose institutions have completed
  legal and privacy use agreements with the AI-READI research programme.

  Communications in Medicine (DICOM) for retinal FLIO, OCT, OCTA and photography; Open
  mHealth for wearable activity monitoring and continuous glucose monitoring; and the
  NASA ASCII File Format Guidelines for Earth Science Data for environmental sensor data.
